C-SEARCH-RESULT-CONTRACT.Name: Honest search-result contract end to end — implementation plan
C-SEARCH-RESULT-CONTRACT.IntentSummary: Make the v1 search-result contract real on the whole path with additive-only producer changes and no consumer migration: src-tauri/src/m013b/search.rs SearchHit grows two additive optional match-bound fields (first-submatch start and end within the delivered snippet, serialized absent when unavailable) filled by both engines under one documented unit convention — UTF-16 code-unit offsets computed at the backend against the delivered snippet text, chosen because both engines' raw spans are byte offsets (regex crate Match spans, rg --json submatch start/end) and the consumer reads JS substring indices, so byte delivery would ship a known-false span on every multi-byte line; the window shim's mt::search-event translation (extracted into a pure zero-import helper module so jsdom can behavior-test it without importing the top-level-await boot shim) maps present bounds into the single array-pair range form [[row, col], [row, col]] the component already reads and deletes the fabricated "column + snippet.length" end, mapping bounds-absent hits to the no-highlight, line-start-cursor zero pair; the ProjectSearch overlay becomes keyboard-operable following the commandPalette zone canon (real focusResults entry, selected-index roving with active class and scrollIntoView, Tab-reachable rows, Escape closing from both contexts, Enter opening the file at the honest match through the same code path as click); quick open normalizes the shim's grouped "filePath" plus "matches" envelope back to string pathnames where didMatch consumes it; one new e2e spec through the tauri-shim fixture proves the Wave-3 criterion — the right file opens at the right match from the keyboard. SearchSessionCoordinator ownership, the SearchEvent envelope, store/search.js, node/ripgrepSearcher.js, node/fileSearcher.js, the typed ipc facade and commandPalette stay untouched.

T-001.Title: Backend bounds contract: failing-first serialization, parity and truncation tests plus the units-convention probe

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Add failing-first inline #[cfg(test)] tests in src-tauri/src/m013b/search.rs that fail against the current tree: (a) search_hit_bounds_wire_form — a SearchHit with known bounds serializes both "matchStart" and "matchEnd" (camelCase wire names via explicit serde rename), while a SearchHit without bounds keeps the struct's established absent-field wire form (no matchStart/matchEnd keys) exactly like SearchEvent's optional error/partial; (b) bounds_parity_across_engines — one fixture searched by both engines (the embedded walker in-process, the rg leg under its existing availability guard) yields identical bounds semantics for the same match: same 0-based start, same exclusive end, same unit, both against the delivered snippet text; (c) the fixture set includes one ASCII line and one multi-byte line (Cyrillic or CJK content) — this is the delivery-baseline probe the spec's units decision rides on: raw engine spans are byte offsets, and the test asserts the delivered bounds point into the delivered snippet so that a JS substring(start, end) of the snippet equals the matched text; (d) truncated-beyond-bounds absence — a match that is not fully inside the delivered (byte-truncated) snippet yields a hit with both bound fields absent, and the batch still delivers the hit itself. Record the failing receipts before implementing.

Record the units-convention decision this plan commits to, and verify it on the delivery baseline inside the parity test: the convention is UTF-16 code-unit offsets (0-based start, exclusive end) computed at the backend against the delivered snippet string — the exact index space of the renderer's substring, exact for BMP and astral content alike — reached from both engines' raw byte spans through one shared conversion (a byte-offset-to-UTF-16-unit helper over the delivered snippet, so both legs stay identical by construction). Unicode scalar-value counts are rejected because they diverge from JS substring indices on astral-plane characters (emoji). If the multi-byte probe on the delivery baseline exposes a contradiction (a platform quirk where the conversion cannot satisfy substring equality), the fallback is the documented ASCII-bounded honesty limitation recorded in this change's file-local CHANGE_SUMMARY and in the graph delta — never a silently shipped known-false span; the walker byte-slice truncation panic itself stays owned by C-SEARCH-ENGINE-PARITY and is not touched here.

T-002.Title: SearchHit honest bounds: additive optional fields filled by both engine legs under one documented unit convention

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Extend SearchHit with exactly two additive optional fields under the struct's established serde style: "pub match_start: Option<u32>," and "pub match_end: Option<u32>," each carrying "#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\", rename = \"matchStart\")]" / "rename = \"matchEnd\"" so unavailability stays an absent wire field and the wire names match the renderer's camelCase convention. No other SearchHit or SearchEvent field changes; no new event kind, channel or envelope field; the partial-flag semantics delivered by #303 are untouched.

Fill the fields in both legs from their exact spans through the shared T-001 conversion against the delivered snippet text: the rg leg takes the first submatch's start and end from the --json submatches array (replacing the "let _ = pattern_len; // reserved for future range-end calc" placeholder and updating the "// First submatch's start column for the column field. Renderer" comment to describe the new contract), and the embedded walker takes each match's own span from matcher.find_iter so every walker hit carries the span of the match it represents. When a match is not fully inside the delivered snippet (walker byte-truncation with the ellipsis marker; defensively for the rg leg too) both fields stay absent — honest-or-absent, never a partial span. The legacy "column" field keeps its current per-leg values untouched (additive-only constraint; its walker/rg one-character start divergence is superseded for rendering by the bounds through the shim and stays recorded here as known debt). Update the file-local MODULE_CONTRACT, MODULE_MAP (SearchHit entry), START_BLOCK_/END_BLOCK_ pairs (unique, matched) and CHANGE_SUMMARY and bump the module version; the T-001 tests turn green with no weakened assertions and all pre-existing search suites stay green.

T-003.Title: Shim range translation: pure helper extraction, failing-first mapping tests, honest array-pair ranges, fabricated end removed

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Record the mapping-test seam choice (the spec leaves extraction-versus-mocked-globals to this plan): the shim module hosts top-level await plus webview/localeLoader dependencies jsdom cannot provide (the C-52 test contract records this), so a real behavior test cannot import install-window-globals.js. Extract the mt::search-event payload translation into a new pure sibling module src/renderer/src/_shims/search-event-translation.js exporting translateSearchEvent(m) — zero imports, no window readers, no side effects — wrapped in a paired // START_BLOCK_SEARCH_RANGE_TRANSLATION / // END_BLOCK_SEARCH_RANGE_TRANSLATION marker; install-window-globals.js keeps its boot shape by statically importing only this zero-dependency helper (safe against the C-52 chunk-pull failure mode, which the static-import ban pins to clipboard modules with import-time window.electron readers) and dispatching "for (const d of translateSearchEvent(m)) handler(event, d)" in the listener branch; the C-52 boot-order pins stay green byte-for-byte.

translateSearchEvent preserves today's funnel shape exactly except for the range form: match envelopes regroup hits per path into { searchId, type: 'match', payload: { filePath, matches } } dispatches (per-path grouping and searchId forwarding unchanged), complete/cancelled/error map to the same type/partial dispatches as today. Each match row's range becomes the single array-pair form from the honest bounds: with present bounds "range: [[row, start], [row, end]]" where row stays "Math.max(0, (h.line || 1) - 1)" and start/end read h.matchStart / h.matchEnd; when both bounds are absent the row maps to the no-highlight, defined-cursor zero pair "range: [[row, 0], [row, 0]]" — the component then renders the full line unhighlighted (empty prefix and highlight spans, full suffix) and opens the cursor at line start; a half-present bounds shape is treated as absent. The fabricated end "(h.column || 0) + (h.snippet ? h.snippet.length : 0)" and the object-form range rows are removed — after this change no producer emits object range rows and the highlighted substring of lineText equals the matched text on every present-bounds hit.

tests/renderer/_shims/install-window-globals.test.js gains the failing-first shim-range-array-form describe (red against today's shim before the helper lands): a realistic mt::search-event feed — two paths, a multi-match line, a bounds-absent hit, a terminal envelope — proves every delivered match carries range as array pairs with honest bounds (highlight substring of lineText equals the matched text), the bounds-absent hit maps to the zero pair, per-path grouping and searchId forwarding are unchanged, and the fabricated end no longer exists in the shim source; it also dynamically imports the helper (no new static imports in the test seam) and adds a source-scan pin that search-event-translation.js contains no static imports of its own. The shim-range-array-form tests must fail before T-003's implementation and pass after; the C-52 pins pass unchanged throughout.

T-005.Title: QuickOpen string pathnames: failing-first string-id pins on the shim-shaped feed and the consumer-side envelope normalization

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: tests/renderer/commands/quickOpen.test.js gains the failing-first quickopen-string-ids case (red today because id becomes an object): with the searcher mocked to deliver the shim-shaped grouped envelope — { filePath: string, matches: [...] } rows through didMatch, plus a plain-string delivery for the tabs path — _doSearch resolves a list whose every id is a pathname string, _getPath receives strings (isChildOfDirectory and window.path.relative keep their string contracts), and executeSubcommand sends mt::open-file-by-window-id with the string pathname. quickOpen-deep.test.js gains the shim-shaped-feed pin for the open invocation path; the existing tabs-only and no-root suites stay green with unchanged assertions.

Implement the normalization consumer-side in src/renderer/src/commands/quickOpen.js where didMatch receives the envelope — "typeof result === 'string'" keeps plain strings, otherwise the grouped envelope's "result.filePath" string pathname is taken and non-string shapes are dropped — so "const item = { id: pathname }" builds a string id and executeSubcommand opens the file again. The raw "searchResult.push(result)" line is gone; the shim gains no per-searchId mode state and the backend files-mode semantics stay untouched (verified against today's content-spawn envelope so the pins rerun unchanged when C-QUICKOPEN-FILES-MODE lands).

The new tests/e2e/project-search.spec.ts (installTauriShim + bootEditor canon) boots the editor, opens the project-search overlay (.project-search-overlay), submits a query whose fixture envelope — delivered through __emitSearchEvent with honest bounds across two files, one multi-match line and one bounds-absent hit — renders the expected rows, and proves the Wave-3 criterion from the keyboard: Enter from the input into the results, arrows to the fixture match line, Enter — the fixture file opens (the mt_open_file double's mt::open-new-tab receipt) carrying the cursor at the fixture match position, and the bounds-absent hit shows no highlight with a defined line-start cursor. AcceptanceVerification.Environment: Baseline is the current green-search1 worktree (branch spec/search-result-contract, base bb68fd6c), executed in that worktree root with cargo and installed node_modules available; no new dependencies are acquired. Tasks run strictly sequentially T-001 through T-007, and the failing-first suites are red on the untouched baseline before their implementations land: the T-001 backend bounds tests fail before T-002, the shim-range-array-form mapping tests fail before T-003, the project-search-keyboard-chain tests fail before T-004, and quickopen-string-ids fails before T-005. Documented plan decisions: the bounds unit is UTF-16 code-unit offsets (0-based start, exclusive end) computed at the backend against the delivered snippet through one shared conversion used by both engine legs — chosen because both legs' raw spans are byte offsets while the consumer reads JS substring indices, byte delivery would be a known-false span on mainstream multi-byte content, and scalar-value counts would diverge on astral characters; the multi-byte parity fixture is the delivery-baseline probe and any contradiction converts the plan to the explicitly documented ASCII-bounded honesty limitation instead of a silent false span. The mapping-test seam is the extracted pure zero-import helper module (src/renderer/src/_shims/search-event-translation.js) because the boot shim's top-level await and webview/localeLoader dependencies cannot load under jsdom; the shim's static import of that zero-dependency helper keeps the C-52 boot-order pins green, and the helper itself carries no static imports (source-scanned). Tab reachability is roving-focused rows (selected row tabindex 0, others -1) with arrows and Enter on the rows. Escape closing is panel-level so both the input and the results contexts close the overlay. Quick-open normalization stays consumer-side with no per-searchId shim state. All commands must pass with no skips, retries, budget increases or weakened assertions; SearchSessionCoordinator keeps sole terminal ownership, store/search.js, node/ripgrepSearcher.js, node/fileSearcher.js, the commandPalette, the typed ipc facade and the in-document find bar stay byte-for-byte untouched, the #289 session-trace and #303 honest-state families plus the C-52 boot-order pins and the e2e search-bar spec pass unchanged, and the e2e spec's receipt is a fixture-envelope proof through the tauri-shim doubles — native rg transport on unmatched platforms, App Store build behavior and owner acceptance stay explicitly open and are never substituted by a shim.
